mainTopic: Offering outside the עזרה: blood sprinklings, the סוכות water libation and its source, and whether libation water has a fixed measure
overview: This amud finishes the משנה about which acts done outside the עזרה make a person חייב. רבי אלעזר adds pouring the סוכות water libation, and רבי נחמיה adds offering the leftover blood. The גמרא first quotes רבא, who says רבי אלעזר agrees that even one sprinkling of blood done outside makes one חייב. The proof is רבי אלעזר's ruling about the יום כיפור sprinklings: if they are interrupted, the כהן גדול picks up from where he stopped. Next, רבי יוחנן says רבי אלעזר's water ruling follows רבי עקיבא, who learns ניסוך המים from the plural ״ונסכיה״. ריש לקיש objects that the water should then copy wine's rules, which are three לוגין and all year round. The גמרא answers with a teaching, given in רבי יוחנן's own name, that ניסוך המים is a הלכה למשה מסיני with its own rules. Finally, a ברייתא gives two views on pouring the water outside. רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that they argue over whether the water has a fixed measure, and רב פפא begins a second explanation that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Pouring the festival water outside makes one liable
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes its previous case with 'חייב', and then רבי אלעזר adds that pouring the סוכות water libation outside the עזרה on the festival also makes one liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...is liable. רבי אלעזר says: Also one who pours the festival water as a libation, on the festival, outside the Temple courtyard, is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes its earlier case and then brings רבי אלעזר's addition: pouring the special סוכות water outside is also an act that makes one חייב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אף' (also) tells us רבי אלעזר is adding to the list of forbidden outside offerings. The ruling only applies to the festival water poured on the festival itself (בחג). That only makes sense if this pouring counts as a real Temple service, and the גמרא will explain why later.

keyTerms.meaning: Liable (here, for the punishment of offering outside the Temple)
One who pours a liquid as a libation on the מזבח
The water set aside for the libation of סוכות
Outside the Temple courtyard (עזרה)

phrases.english: is liable.
Rabbi Elazar says:
Also one who pours the water of the festival as a libation
on the festival, outside, is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: אַף הַמְנַסֵּךְ מֵי הֶחָג בֶּחָג בַּחוּץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of liable outside offerings from the earlier part of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אלעזר, pouring the סוכות water libation outside the עזרה on the festival makes one חייב.

steps.title: Offering the leftover blood outside makes one liable
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה adds that one who offers the leftover blood outside the עזרה is also liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נחמיה says: The leftover blood that one offered outside makes him liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with another addition. רבי נחמיה says that even pouring out the leftover blood outside the עזרה makes one חייב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the main sprinklings, the leftover blood (שירי הדם) is poured at the base of the מזבח. רבי נחמיה treats that pouring as a real service. So doing it outside counts as offering outside.

keyTerms.meaning: The leftover blood that remains after the required sprinklings
That one offered them

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה lists two extra cases of outside liability: the סוכות water (רבי אלעזר) and the leftover blood (רבי נחמיה).

phrases.english: Rabbi Nechemya says:
The leftover blood that one offered
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the corrected wording is the one in square brackets, meaning 'that one offered them.'

phrases.english: outside, he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another opinion that widens the list of liable outside offerings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי נחמיה, offering the שירי הדם outside makes one חייב.

steps.title: רבא: רבי אלעזר agrees about blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with רבא's statement that רבי אלעזר agrees one is liable when it comes to sprinkling blood outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבא said: And רבי אלעזר agrees regarding blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. רבא tells us that on the matter of blood sprinklings, רבי אלעזר agrees that one is liable for doing them outside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'agrees' (מודה) means רבי אלעזר usually holds a more lenient rule, generally requiring a complete offering before one is liable. רבא is saying blood is different: even part of the sprinklings done outside makes one חייב. The next step brings the proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for גמרא; marks where the גמרא's discussion begins
And he agrees (admits a point despite his general view)
Regarding blood (the sprinklings of an offering's blood)

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rava said:
And Rabbi Elazar agrees regarding blood.
phrases.notes: 'Agrees' means that here he admits something beyond his usual position: one sprinkling of blood is enough for liability.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: וּמוֹדֶה רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּדָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא by clarifying how far רבי אלעזר's view reaches, specifically for blood.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר agrees that one is liable for sprinkling blood outside, even when only part of the sprinklings is done.

steps.title: Proof: each sprinkling stands on its own
steps.stepSummary: A teaching about the יום כיפור service shows that רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון hold that when blood spills partway through, the כהן גדול continues from where he stopped.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון say: From the place where he stopped, there he begins.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves רבא's claim. It quotes a teaching where רבי אלעזר says that if the sprinkling of blood is interrupted, the כהן just picks up where he left off.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is about the many יום כיפור sprinklings. If the blood spills and new blood is brought, the כהן does not start over. That shows each sprinkling counts as a full act by itself. So doing even one sprinkling outside makes one חייב, which is exactly רבא's point.

keyTerms.meaning: Where he stopped
He begins

steps.whatToRemember: Because each sprinkling of blood counts by itself, רבי אלעזר holds one is liable even for a single sprinkling done outside.

phrases.english: As it is taught:
Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon say:
From the place where he stopped, he begins.
phrases.notes: This is about the יום כיפור blood sprinklings, when the blood spilled partway through and new blood had to be brought.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמְרִים: מִמָּקוֹם שֶׁפָּסַק הוּא מַתְחִיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source that supports רבא's statement.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that רבי אלעזר agrees one is liable for blood sprinklings outside.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling of רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון that after an interruption the כהן continues from where he stopped, so each sprinkling is an independent act.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר follows his teacher רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי אלעזר's ruling about the festival water again. רבי יוחנן explains that it follows רבי עקיבא, who holds that the water libation is from the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: Also one who pours the festival water on the festival outside. רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי מנחם יודפאה: רבי אלעזר said this following the view of his teacher רבי עקיבא, who said: The water libation is from the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the second ruling in the משנה, quoting it again in order to explain it. רבי יוחנן tells us the reason: רבי אלעזר follows רבי עקיבא's view that ניסוך המים is a Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One is liable for offering outside only for a real Torah-level service. So if the water libation were just a rabbinic practice, pouring it outside would not make one חייב. Linking רבי אלעזר to רבי עקיבא explains how his ruling can work.

keyTerms.meaning: Following the approach or view of
His teacher
The pouring of water on the מזבח during סוכות
From the Torah (a Torah-level law, not rabbinic)

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says:
Also one who pours the festival water as a libation, on the festival, outside.
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the משנה again so it can explain it. The word in square brackets is part of the corrected wording.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said
in the name of Rabbi Menachem Yodfa'a:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר – בְּשִׁטַּת רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא רַבּוֹ אֲמָרָהּ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said it following the view of Rabbi Akiva, his teacher,
who said: The water libation is from the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מְנַחֵם יוֹדְפָאָה: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּשִׁטַּת רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא רַבּוֹ אֲמָרָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the topic of blood to explaining רבי אלעזר's second ruling in the משנה, about the festival water.
steps.whyThisMatters: Liability for offering outside depends on the act being a real Torah service, so the status of ניסוך המים decides whether רבי אלעזר's ruling holds.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר's ruling follows רבי עקיבא, who holds that ניסוך המים is a Torah law.

steps.title: Proof from the plural word 'its libations'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows רבי עקיבא learning from the plural ״ונסכיה״ that the פסוק refers to two libations, water and wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: רבי עקיבא says: 'And its libations', the פסוק is speaking of two libations, one the water libation and one the wine libation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source showing that רבי עקיבא really holds the water libation is from the Torah. He learns it from a plural word in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'its libations' in the plural, not just 'its libation'. רבי עקיבא reads the extra plural as pointing to a second libation besides the usual wine: the סוכות water. This makes ניסוך המים a Torah law, so pouring it outside makes one חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: And its libations (plural)
The פסוק is speaking about
The wine libation that goes with offerings

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר makes one liable for pouring the festival water outside because, like his teacher רבי עקיבא, he holds that ניסוך המים comes from the Torah. רבי עקיבא learns this from the plural ״ונסכיה״.

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Akiva says:
'And its libations':
phrases.notes: במדבר 29:31. The point is that the word is plural.

phrases.english: the verse is speaking of two libations:
one is the water libation,
and one is the wine libation.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: וּנְסָכֶיהָ בִּשְׁנֵי נִיסּוּכִים הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the claim that רבי עקיבא holds ניסוך המים is from the Torah.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's statement that רבי עקיבא holds ניסוך המים is a Torah law.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי עקיבא's reading of the plural ״ונסכיה״ (במדבר 29:31) as two libations, water and wine.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: If water is learned from wine, it should follow wine's rules
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש challenges רבי יוחנן. If רבי אלעזר learns water from wine like רבי עקיבא, then water should need three לוגין and should apply all year, like wine. But רבי אלעזר says neither.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said to רבי יוחנן: If water is learned from wine, then just as wine needs three לוגין, water should need three לוגין. But רבי אלעזר just says 'festival water,' with no amount! And just as wine applies all year round, water should apply all year round. But רבי אלעזר says 'on the festival'!
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש attacks רבי יוחנן's claim that רבי אלעזר follows רבי עקיבא. He points out two ways that רבי אלעזר's ruling does not match the rules of wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא learns water and wine from the same word ״ונסכיה״, so the two should share the same rules. Wine needs three לוגין and can be poured any day of the year. רבי אלעזר says nothing about an amount and limits the liability to the חג, so he seems not to be learning water from wine at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Just as there... so too here (comparing two cases)
Three לוג, the amount used for the wine libation
The rest of the days of the year

steps.confusionAlert: ריש לקיש is not arguing about the הלכה of wine. He is saying that if two things are learned from one word, they should have the same rules, and רבי אלעזר's ruling shows that they don't.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Reish Lakish said to Rabbi Yochanan:
If so, just as there it is three log,
phrases.notes: "There" means wine. If water is learned from the same word as wine, it should copy wine's rules.

phrases.english: so too here it should be three log?!
But Rabbi Elazar says "water of the festival"!
phrases.notes: He gives no amount, so it sounds like any amount of festival water counts.

phrases.aramaic: אִי – מָה לְהַלָּן בִּשְׁאָר יְמוֹת הַשָּׁנָה,
phrases.english: If so, just as there it applies during the rest of the days of the year,
so too here it should apply during the rest of the days of the year?!
But Rabbi Elazar says "on the festival"!
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are added in the corrected wording.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אִי – מָה לְהַלָּן שְׁלֹשֶׁת לוּגִּין, אַף כָּאן שְׁלֹשֶׁת לוּגִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's explanation from Step 5, which was based on רבי עקיבא's reading in Step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that רבי אלעזר follows רבי עקיבא, who learns water and wine together.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If water is learned from wine, it should share wine's rules: three לוגין and liability all year. רבי אלעזר requires neither, so he cannot be learning water from wine.

steps.title: A forgotten teaching: the water libation is a הלכה למשה מסיני
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא responds that a teaching was overlooked: רבי אסי's report in the name of רבי יוחנן that ניסוך המים is a הלכה למשה מסיני. Because it has its own source, it does not have to copy the rules of wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: He forgot what רבי אסי said. רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן, quoting רבי נחוניא איש בקעת בית חורתן: ten saplings, the willow, and the water libation are each a הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers ריש לקיש's question by pointing to an overlooked teaching, reported in רבי יוחנן's own name, that the water libation is a הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ניסוך המים is a הלכה למשה מסיני, its details come from that tradition and not from the rules of wine. So the water libation can be limited to the חג and does not need to follow wine's three לוגין. This removes ריש לקיש's challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: It escaped him; he forgot it
A law handed down orally to משה at Sinai, not learned from a פסוק
Ten saplings
The willow used in the בית המקדש on סוכות
The water libation poured on the מזבח on סוכות

steps.whatToRemember: ניסוך המים is a הלכה למשה מסיני, so its rules do not have to match the wine libation.

phrases.english: That which Rabbi Asi said escaped him;
phrases.notes: The גמרא doesn't say who 'him' is. Notice the teaching is given in רבי יוחנן's own name.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
phrases.english: as Rabbi Asi said that Rabbi Yochanan said

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי נְחוּנְיָא אִישׁ בִּקְעַת בֵּית חוֹרְתָן:
phrases.english: in the name of Rabbi Nechunya, a man of the valley of Beit Chortan:
Ten saplings, the willow, and the water libation –
are a halacha given to Moshe from Sinai.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers ריש לקיש's challenge from Step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings in an outside teaching that gives ניסוך המים its own source.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Water is learned from wine, so it must follow wine's rules.
steps.terutzMaskana: The water libation is a הלכה למשה מסיני and has its own rules, so it can be limited to the חג without a three לוג minimum.

steps.title: A ברייתא on pouring three לוגין of water outside on סוכות
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: the תנא קמא says one who pours three לוגין of water outside on the חג is liable. רבי אלעזר says he is liable if he filled the water for the sake of the חג.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: One who pours three לוגין of water outside on the festival is liable. רבי אלעזר (son of רבי שמעון) says: If he filled them for the sake of the festival, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about pouring festival water outside the עזרה. Two opinions are given, and the difference between them is not yet clear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא focuses on the amount poured, three לוגין. רבי אלעזר focuses on whether the water was filled for the חג. Their wordings differ, and this sets up the question of what practical difference there is between them.

keyTerms.meaning: One who pours a libation
Outside the עזרה
He filled them, in a כלי שרת, for the sake of the חג

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
One who pours as a libation three log of water
on the festival, outside, is liable.
Rabbi Elazar (son of Rabbi Shimon) says:
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets, so read it simply as רבי אלעזר.

phrases.english: If he filled them for the sake of the festival, he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַמְנַסֵּךְ שְׁלֹשֶׁת לוּגִּין מַיִם בֶּחָג בַּחוּץ – חַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic with a ברייתא about pouring festival water outside the עזרה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תנא קמא: pouring three לוגין of water outside on the חג makes one liable. רבי אלעזר: one is liable if the water was filled for the sake of the חג.

steps.title: What is the difference between the two opinions?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between the תנא קמא and רבי אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where the two opinions in the ברייתא actually disagree. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions seem to agree that pouring festival water outside makes one liable. The גמרא wants to find a case where they would actually rule differently.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the ברייתא brought in Step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical case where the תנא קמא and רבי אלעזר would rule differently.

steps.title: They argue whether the water has a fixed measure
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that they disagree about whether there is a fixed measure for the water.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: They disagree about whether water has a fixed measure.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers the question. The two opinions argue about whether the libation water has a set measure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא holds there is no fixed measure, so even water filled in a larger amount becomes holy, and pouring three לוגין of it outside makes one liable. רבי אלעזר holds there is a fixed measure, so filling more than three לוגין does not make the water holy, and one is liable only if exactly the right amount was filled for the חג.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a fixed measure for the water
They disagree

steps.whatToRemember: The two opinions in the ברייתא argue about whether libation water has a fixed measure. This decides whether too much water filled in the כלי still becomes holy.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
They disagree about whether there is a fixed measure for water.
phrases.notes: The question is whether filling more than the right amount still makes the water holy for the libation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: בְּיֵשׁ שִׁיעוּר בְּמַיִם קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in Step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dispute is about whether there is a fixed measure for libation water, which decides whether an oversized filling still becomes holy.

steps.title: רב פפא begins a second answer
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא is introduced as offering another explanation of the difference between the תנא קמא and רבי אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a second answer to the question of what the practical difference is between the תנא קמא and רבי אלעזר. Only the opening words appear here, and רב פפא's actual explanation comes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן בר יצחק already said the argument is about whether there is a fixed measure for the water. When a new אמורא is introduced right after an answer like this, he usually explains the disagreement a different way. To see what רב פפא's view is, keep reading into the next line.
